strategic_horizon.terminal_goal: Build a personal weak-network VPN with UDP/datagram-like earliest-complete inner delivery over WBD-owned TCP-shaped FakeTCP, a 100 Mbit/s weak-link release ceiling, shared username/password admission for multiple independent LiveID sessions, OpenWrt TPROXY capture, and Windows TUN/Wintun-class capture.
strategic_horizon.current_milestone: Shared-account two-session clean-path fan-out and the first 40 Mbit/s aggregate weak-link characterization are qualified. Keep protocol/FEC semantics frozen while measuring the safe aggregate offered-load ceiling on the 100 Mbit/s shared bottleneck, then freeze protocol and move to final OpenWrt/Windows end-to-end integration.
strategic_horizon.local_optimization_stop_rule: Prioritize first-complete inner datagram delivery and balanced independent sessions. Never gate available systematic data on cumulative TCP repair, do not add multi-tenant identity complexity, and do not retune fixed 20:20 from a single load point before the 100 Mbit/s shared-link load ceiling is measured.

continuation_cursor.last_completed_action: Qualified same-account two-session fan-out through one public FakeTCP listener for FEC off and fixed 20:20, added DTLS-protected PING/PONG/CLOSE lifecycle with a 15s client keepalive and 90s server idle lease, fixed the bounded test activation race, and completed the first shared 100 Mbit/s two-session load characterization. Authoritative mux-load run 32918572671 passed all four network jobs plus aggregate with setup loss 0 and measured random loss 20%. At 40 Mbit/s aggregate inner offered, RTT20 off delivered 0.8022 / 32.083 Mbit/s / p99 11.061ms versus fixed20:20 1.0000 / 39.994 Mbit/s / p99 20.678ms; RTT100 off delivered 0.8062 / 32.242 Mbit/s / p99 50.770ms versus fixed20:20 1.0000 / 39.994 Mbit/s / p99 61.185ms. Fixed plaintext expansion measured 2.1622x and 2.1597x. Results are recorded in docs/benchmarks/v2-mux-two-session-100m.md. Handoff architecture assertions were also aligned with the now-qualified M8A/M8B/M8C roadmap state and the new mux benchmark evidence.
continuation_cursor.current_task: Find the safe aggregate inner offered-load ceiling for two simultaneous same-account sessions on the 100 Mbit/s shared weak link without changing the qualified mux, legacy FakeTCP default, DTLS worker model, or fixed 20:20 semantics.
continuation_cursor.why_now: At 20% measured random loss, fixed 20:20 recovered both 20 and 100 ms RTT cases from about 80% delivery to 100%, but its measured LINK->DTLS plaintext expansion is about 2.16x and costs roughly 16-18% more sampled CPU, 26-33% more peak RSS, and about 10ms more p99. Forty Mbit/s aggregate inner therefore already consumes roughly the mid-80-Mbit/s range before DTLS/FakeTCP overhead. The next product risk is saturation/queue collapse, not correctness of session fan-out.
continuation_cursor.done_when: A paired aggregate-load sweep on the same two-session topology identifies the highest sustainable inner offered rate at RTT 20/100 ms with measured 20% random loss, using setup loss 0 and loss only during the offered interval. Record delivery/goodput/p50/p99, per-session balance, CPU/RSS, exact systematic/repair plaintext bytes, FakeTCP retransmit bytes and shared qdisc drops. Do not freeze protocol or begin final platform VPN integration until the ceiling and a conservative release operating point are documented.
continuation_cursor.next_atomic_action: Extend scripts/bench_mux_two_session_100m.py / mux-load-100m workflow into a load sweep at aggregate inner 40 -> 60 -> 80 Mbit/s (20 -> 30 -> 40 per session), RTT 20/100 ms, measured random loss 20%, preserving setup_loss_pct=0 and the existing exact plaintext meter. Start with fixed 20:20 plus an off-mode control at each RTT/load; stop increasing load when persistent queue/tail collapse or materially unfair session delivery appears. Do not retune FEC or recovery during this sweep.

udp_like_status.outer_semantics: WBD-owned TCP-shaped raw carrier with legacy shadow recovery as the product default. SACK/RACK remains explicit experimental research. Complete inner datagram delivery never waits for cumulative TCP ACK or repair.
udp_like_status.fec_status: Live negotiation admits FEC off or fixed systematic 20:20 tail-RS. Surviving systematic sources stream immediately and missing originals reconstruct from repair shards; no runtime config epoch or adaptive retune is qualified.
udp_like_status.two_client_clean_gate: GitHub Actions fullstack-mux-two-client run 32911866748 SUCCESS for both FEC off and fixed 20:20: two distinct tickets from one shared account, one public FakeTCP listener, two inherited-fd wolfSSL DTLS workers, two independent LINK/LiveID sessions, concurrent unique application echoes with no cross-session routing.
udp_like_status.two_session_load_gate: GitHub Actions mux-load-100m run 32918572671 SUCCESS at 100 Mbit/s shared link, two simultaneous 20 Mbit/s inner streams, RTT 20/100 ms, setup loss 0 and measurement random loss 20%. Fixed 20:20 delivered 100% at both RTTs versus off about 80%; p99 increased by 9.617/10.415ms and exact fixed plaintext expansion was 2.1622x/2.1597x.
udp_like_status.lifecycle: Client sends DTLS-protected WBD PING after 15s idle, handles PONG/CLOSE, and on normal stop flushes FEC then best-effort CLOSE_NORMAL. Shared link server refreshes active leases on data/control/service traffic, echoes lifecycle control via the existing state machine, and reclaims idle LiveID slots after a default 90s lease.
udp_like_status.memory_policy: Performance first: retain bounded independent state per LiveID and never gate new inner datagrams on pending repair depth merely to save memory.
udp_like_status.capacity_policy: Active release qualification uses a 100 Mbit/s weak shared link or lower. The current 40 Mbit/s aggregate inner point is qualified but is not yet the safe load ceiling.

product_policy.link_setup: Reality-like TLS front is connection setup only. Recognized same-entry TLS authenticates the shared username/password and issues a fresh one-time ticket; FakeTCP/DTLS then performs ticket bind and immutable LINK_INIT/LINK_ACCEPT. Sustained VPN payload never uses the front TCP stream.
product_policy.fec: Association setup admits off or fixed systematic 20:20 tail-RS. No runtime FEC config epoch; adaptive/intermediate profiles remain research until separately qualified.
product_policy.accounts: One configured shared username/password may authenticate multiple simultaneous devices. Every login gets a distinct random ticket/LiveID; live routing and FEC state are keyed by LiveID/peer, never username.
product_policy.recovery: FakeTCP product default is legacy shadow recovery. sack-rack remains opt-in experimental/diagnostic and is not a release default.
product_policy.certificate_policy: Personal client may explicitly disable certificate-chain and hostname verification for both front TLS and DTLS while encryption remains enabled and logs disclose the verification mode.
product_policy.routing: OpenWrt final capture is TPROXY plus policy routing and underlay escape; Windows final capture is TUN/Wintun-class with endpoint escape. Linux TUN remains a regression harness.
product_policy.release_gate: After protocol/unit/pcap/100M weak-link and load-ceiling gates are green, freeze protocol, then require one clean end-to-end VPN success on OpenWrt TPROXY and one on Windows TUN including real DNS/TCP/UDP application traffic, underlay escape and cleanup/restoration.
